title: Food Safety & Quality Management System Governance

requirements.title: Written Food Safety ****&**** Quality Policy
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a written Food Safety & Quality Policy, signed by senior leadership, communicated to all personnel, and reviewed at least annually.
requirements.source: MFI Supplier Expectation Manual governance section (analog); GFSI Code Ed. 9/SQF Code Ed. 10 §2.1.1 pattern
requirements.auditorNote: No direct 21 CFR 117 equivalent. Verify signature is current-year and policy references cannabis-specific hazards, not generic food-safety boilerplate.

requirements.title: Documented management commitment
requirements.statement: Facility demonstrates documented management commitment to food safety/quality: budget allocation, staffing levels, and leadership participation in food safety meetings are evidenced.
requirements.auditorNote: Interview site leadership directly, not just the QA manager. Look for capital spend on sanitation/EMP/testing in the last 12 months as objective evidence.

requirements.title: Functionally independent QA reporting line
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a current organizational chart identifying food safety/quality reporting lines, with QA/QC functionally independent from Production/Operations management.
requirements.source: MFI Supplier Expectation Manual; GFSI structural-independence principle
requirements.auditorNote: Flag as a finding if QA reports through Plant Manager/Operations rather than a separate quality or corporate line.

requirements.title: Qualified individual with PCQI-equivalent training
requirements.statement: Facility designates a qualified individual responsible for food safety/quality oversight, with documented training/qualifications equivalent to a PCQI standard, even where state cannabis law does not explicitly require PCQI certification.
requirements.states: CO, CA, WA, MO, AR (UNIV best practice)
requirements.auditorNote: Single most important crosswalk point in the program: infused edibles/tinctures are 'food' for adulteration purposes even where FDA does not regulate cannabis itself. Topicals are the exception.

requirements.title: Risk-based internal audit program
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented, risk-based internal audit program covering GMP, sanitation, and process control areas at a minimum annual frequency, with findings tracked to closure.
requirements.source: MFI Supplier Expectation Manual; SQF Code Ed. 10 §2.4 pattern; CO annual audit mandate
requirements.auditorNote: For Colorado, cross-reference whether the internal audit calendar feeds the mandatory annual third-party audit, or runs as a disconnected, duplicate exercise.

requirements.title: Semi-annual management review
requirements.statement: Facility conducts documented management review of food safety/quality performance (audit results, complaints, recalls/mock recalls, EMP trends, testing failures) at a minimum semi-annual frequency.
requirements.auditorNote: Look for evidence of action, not just meeting minutes.

requirements.title: Current, valid, unencumbered state licensure
requirements.statement: Facility maintains current, valid state cannabis manufacturing/processing licensure with no active suspensions, revocation proceedings, or unresolved compliance holds, verified against the state regulatory body's public license lookup.
requirements.source: CO MED/Hemp Division; CA DCC; WA LCB; MO DHSS/DCR; AR ABC/Cannabis Division
requirements.auditorNote: Pre-audit desk check, independently verified against the state's public database, not just a paper license pulled on-site.

requirements.title: Regulatory change management process
requirements.statement: Facility has a documented process for monitoring, evaluating, and implementing changes to applicable state cannabis regulations and food safety code updates.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask specifically how the facility learned of and responded to the most recent rule change in their state.

requirements.title: Document control system
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a document control system ensuring current-version SOPs/records are in use at point-of-use, obsolete versions are retired/marked, and records are legible, complete, and attributable.
requirements.source: 21 CFR 117.190; MFI Supplier Expectation Manual document control section
requirements.auditorNote: Check for version-control drift on the floor against the QA office's master file.

requirements.title: Record retention meeting the longer of federal or state minimums
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented record retention program meeting the longer of: state cannabis regulatory retention period, or 21 CFR 117.310 food record retention minimums.
requirements.auditorNote: State cannabis retention periods frequently exceed the federal minimum for track-and-trace/testing records.

requirements.title: Grounds maintained against pest attraction
requirements.statement: Grounds are maintained to minimize pest attraction and harborage: no standing water, overgrown vegetation, debris accumulation, or improperly stored equipment adjacent to the building.
requirements.auditorNote: Walk the full perimeter, including areas near HVAC intakes and dumpster pads.

requirements.title: Exterior sealed against pest entry
requirements.statement: Facility exterior (walls, roof, foundation) is maintained to prevent pest entry and environmental contamination; no unsealed gaps, holes, or deteriorated construction materials.
requirements.auditorNote: Pay particular attention to dock doors, conduit penetrations, and roofline.

requirements.title: Sound, cleanable interior construction
requirements.statement: Plant construction (floors, walls, ceilings) is of sound, durable, cleanable material appropriate to the operation; no unsealed porous surfaces, cracked flooring, or exposed insulation in processing/storage areas.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify floor coating and wall material were actually upgraded to washdown-rated finish in retrofit facilities, not just painted over.

requirements.title: Adequate, shielded lighting
requirements.statement: Adequate lighting is provided in all areas where food/product is examined, processed, or stored, and light fixtures over exposed product are shatter-resistant or shielded.
requirements.auditorNote: Check specifically over open extraction vessels, infusion kettles, and packaging lines, and smaller ancillary rooms.

requirements.title: Ventilation adequate to control odor, vapor, and condensation
requirements.statement: Adequate ventilation is provided to minimize odors, vapors (including solvent vapors in extraction areas), and condensation that could contribute to contamination.
requirements.auditorNote: Overlaps with the odor-control-plan requirement (2.12) but is distinct — score independently.

requirements.title: Pest exclusion at openings
requirements.statement: Screening, air curtains, or other effective means are used to minimize pest/insect entry at doors, windows, and other openings kept open for operational reasons.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify strip curtains or air curtains are functional, not just installed and broken.

requirements.title: Traffic-flow separation between raw intake and finished product
requirements.statement: Facility layout provides adequate separation between raw/unsanitized cannabis material intake and finished infused-product areas to prevent cross-contamination.
requirements.auditorNote: Trace actual product and personnel flow on a walkthrough rather than relying on a posted flow diagram.

requirements.title: Zone-based risk classification and separation
requirements.statement: Where zone-based risk classification is used (Zone 1 exposed product / Zone 2 immediately adjacent / Zone 3 general production / Zone 4 non-production), physical or procedural controls enforce zone separation.
requirements.source: FDA EMP guidance; MFI EMP zone-map expectation
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-reference with the EMP zone map in Section 5; don't double-score.

requirements.title: Separation of non-production areas
requirements.statement: Non-production areas (employee break rooms, restrooms, offices) are physically separated from production/storage areas such that they do not create a contamination pathway.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask about air-handling separation specifically where break rooms were carved out of former grow rooms.

requirements.title: Adequate plumbing and backflow prevention
requirements.statement: Plumbing is of adequate size/design, properly conveys sewage/liquid waste, and does not constitute a source of contamination (no cross-connections, adequate floor drainage, backflow prevention devices installed and tested).
requirements.auditorNote: Request backflow prevention device testing records, not just visual presence of the device.

requirements.title: Toxic material storage separation
requirements.statement: Toxic materials (cleaning chemicals, pesticides, lubricants, extraction solvents) are identified, stored, and labeled to prevent contamination of product, food-contact surfaces, or packaging; storage is physically separated from production/storage areas.
requirements.auditorNote: For extraction-equipped facilities, verify bulk solvent storage meets fire code/hazmat separation in addition to food-contamination separation.

requirements.title: Certified odor control plan
requirements.statement: Facility has developed, implemented, and maintains a documented odor control plan, reviewed and certified as sufficient by a professional engineer or certified industrial hygienist prior to commencing operations; compliant with local odor ordinances.
requirements.states: CO, CA, WA (verify current local ordinance)
requirements.auditorNote: Odor ordinances are frequently municipal, not state-level — verify live at each audit.

requirements.title: Security infrastructure coexisting with sanitation zoning
requirements.statement: Facility design accommodates required security infrastructure (video surveillance, intrusion detection, vault/safe storage) per state cannabis licensing security requirements, without compromising food-safety traffic-flow or sanitation zoning.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify camera housings don't create sanitation blind spots over exposed product zones.

requirements.title: Adequately sized, non-commingled storage
requirements.statement: Facility maintains adequate, designated space for cannabis and non-cannabis ingredient/material storage that prevents commingling, physical damage, and temperature/humidity excursion, sized appropriately for actual production volume.
requirements.auditorNote: Over-capacity storage (product staged in aisles/hallways) is a frequent finding in scaling operations.

requirements.title: Cleanable, food-grade equipment construction
requirements.statement: Equipment and utensils are designed, constructed, and installed to facilitate cleaning and maintenance; food-contact surfaces are smooth, non-porous, non-toxic, and free of pits, cracks, or crevices.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify food-contact surfaces on repurposed industrial/pharma equipment are actually food-grade.

requirements.title: Chemical-compatible food-contact surfaces
requirements.statement: Food-contact surfaces are corrosion-resistant and compatible with the product, cleaning compounds, and sanitizing agents used.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify against actual chemical inventory, not just a spec sheet.

requirements.title: Smoothly bonded seams
requirements.statement: Seams on food-contact surfaces are smoothly bonded or maintained to minimize accumulation of food particles, dirt, and organic matter.
requirements.auditorNote: Inspect welds under magnification/flashlight where visual access allows.

requirements.title: Adequate service clearance
requirements.statement: Equipment in areas where food is manipulated is installed to allow adequate access for cleaning and inspection (clearance from walls/floors, or is readily movable).
requirements.auditorNote: Measure clearance where it looks marginal rather than estimating visually.

requirements.title: Contamination-protective holding and conveying systems
requirements.statement: Holding, conveying, and storage systems (hoppers, augers, piping, tanks) are designed to protect product from contamination and are constructed of materials that do not adulterate the product.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify piping runs, not just vessels, meet food-grade standard for beverage lines.

requirements.title: Accurate, maintained measuring instruments
requirements.statement: Instruments and controls used for measuring, regulating, or recording temperatures, pH, water activity, or other critical parameters are accurate, precise, and adequately maintained.
requirements.auditorNote: Feeds into the calibration program (3.08); score separately.

requirements.title: Treated compressed gases
requirements.statement: Compressed air or other gases introduced into food or used to clean food-contact surfaces/equipment are treated to prevent contamination (filtered, oil-free where applicable).
requirements.auditorNote: Directly relevant to CO2 extraction systems and pneumatic product-transfer lines.

requirements.title: Documented calibration program
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented equipment calibration program (scales, thermometers, pH meters, water activity meters, dosing/metering equipment) with defined frequency, tolerance, and out-of-tolerance corrective action.
requirements.auditorNote: Dosing/metering equipment calibration carries higher stakes since it supports label-claim accuracy.

requirements.title: Qualified dosing/homogenization equipment
requirements.statement: Dosing, metering, and homogenization equipment used to achieve uniform cannabinoid distribution is qualified/validated at installation and requalified after any modification, relocation, or major maintenance event.
requirements.source: WAC 314-55-077(8) homogenization mandate + standard equipment-validation practice
requirements.auditorNote: Request batch-uniformity validation study documentation, not just a maintenance log.

requirements.title: Equipment maintained free of improvised repairs
requirements.statement: Utensils and equipment used in producing, holding, or conveying food are maintained in a state of repair sufficient to prevent contamination (no chipped, cracked, corroded, or improvised/jury-rigged components).
requirements.auditorNote: Watch for duct-tape, zip-tie, or improvised repairs.

requirements.title: Controlled single-service articles
requirements.statement: Single-service and single-use articles (where used) are stored, handled, and dispensed to protect against contamination, and are not reused.
requirements.auditorNote: Status conditional on whether the facility's process uses single-service articles.

requirements.title: Preventive maintenance program with tracked completion
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented preventive maintenance (PM) program for all production equipment, distinct from reactive/breakdown maintenance, with PM schedules tracked to completion.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask for the trailing-12-month PM completion rate, not just the schedule.

requirements.title: Fire/safety-code-certified extraction equipment
requirements.statement: Extraction equipment (CO2, ethanol, hydrocarbon, or other solvent-based systems) is designed, installed, and certified in accordance with applicable fire/safety code in addition to food-contact material standards.
requirements.states: CO, CA, WA, MO, AR (verify local fire code adoption)
requirements.source: NFPA 1 / local fire marshal certification requirements
requirements.auditorNote: Document as a critical finding with a referral note; final compliance rests with the fire marshal.

requirements.title: Validated CIP/COP cleaning
requirements.statement: Equipment cleaning-in-place (CIP) or clean-out-of-place (COP) systems are validated to achieve effective residue removal, with validation repeated after any significant equipment or process change.
requirements.auditorNote: Benchmark against a documented CIP sequence (pre-rinse, alkaline wash, intermediate rinse, acid rinse, sanitizer with ATP verification).

requirements.title: Written Master Sanitation Schedule
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a written Master Sanitation Schedule (MSS) identifying all equipment, surfaces, and areas requiring cleaning/sanitizing, with defined frequency, method, and responsible party for each item.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the MSS covers ancillary equipment (staging carts, overflow racks) often omitted.

requirements.title: Detailed SSOPs
requirements.statement: Facility maintains written Sanitation Standard Operating Procedures (SSOPs) for each cleaning task on the MSS, specifying disassembly steps, chemical concentration, contact time, water temperature, and reassembly/verification steps.
requirements.auditorNote: Generic 'clean and sanitize equipment' language is functionally non-compliant.

requirements.title: Chemicals used per label and verified in practice
requirements.statement: Cleaning compounds, sanitizing agents, and other chemicals used are safe and effective for their intended use, and are used in accordance with label instructions (concentration, contact time, temperature).
requirements.auditorNote: Verify in-use sanitizer concentration with test strips during the walkthrough.

requirements.title: Approved chemical list with current SDS
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented chemical approval program: all cleaning/sanitizing chemicals in use are on an approved list, with current Safety Data Sheets (SDS) on file and accessible.
requirements.auditorNote: Physically reconcile the chemical inventory against the approved list to catch unapproved substitutions.

requirements.title: Contemporaneous, supervisor-verified sanitation records
requirements.statement: Sanitation records (cleaning logs, pre-operational inspection results) are completed contemporaneously, are legible and complete, and are reviewed/verified by a supervisor or QA designee.
requirements.auditorNote: Watch for signs of batch-completed records suggesting after-the-fact documentation.

requirements.title: Pre-operational inspections with defined criteria
requirements.statement: Pre-operational sanitation inspections are conducted prior to the start of production, covering food-contact surfaces, equipment, and the immediate production environment, with defined pass/fail criteria and corrective action for failures.
requirements.auditorNote: Observe an actual pre-op inspection where audit timing allows.

requirements.title: Objective cleaning-effectiveness verification
requirements.statement: Verification of cleaning effectiveness is performed using an objective method (ATP bioluminescence swabbing, visual inspection checklist, or micro swabbing) with defined acceptance thresholds and corrective action for failing results.
requirements.auditorNote: Benchmark against a threshold such as ≤100 RLU (Hygiena SystemSURE Plus).

requirements.title: Objective chemical-concentration verification
requirements.statement: Sanitation chemical concentrations are verified using an objective testing method (test strips, titration, or automated dispensing with concentration monitoring) at a defined frequency, not solely by visual/color estimation.
requirements.auditorNote: Automated dispensing still needs a periodic independent verification check.

requirements.title: Documented chemical/method approval process
requirements.statement: Facility has a documented process for evaluating and approving new cleaning chemicals or sanitation methods prior to implementation, including compatibility assessment with equipment materials and product safety.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the approval process for the facility's most recently added chemical.

requirements.title: Zone-designated cleaning tools
requirements.statement: Cleaning tools (brushes, scrapers, cloths, mops) are color-coded or otherwise designated by zone/area to prevent cross-contamination between zones.
requirements.category: MAND where zone separation applies; VOL otherwise
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 2.08.

requirements.title: Sanitary storage of cleaning tools
requirements.statement: Cleaning tools and equipment (brushes, mops, buckets) are themselves cleaned, sanitized, and stored in a manner that prevents them from becoming a contamination source.
requirements.auditorNote: Check under sinks and in janitorial closets for wet-stored tools.

requirements.title: Non-production-area sanitation on the schedule
requirements.statement: Non-production sanitation (restrooms, break rooms, locker rooms, employee entrances) is included on the Master Sanitation Schedule with defined frequency, even though these are not food-contact areas.
requirements.auditorNote: Frequently the weakest link precisely because it's perceived as 'not food safety.'

requirements.title: Documented pathogen environmental control response
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented Listeria/pathogen environmental control program response plan, distinct from routine sanitation, triggered by positive environmental monitoring results.
requirements.source: FDA EMP guidance; MFI EMP corrective action expectation
requirements.auditorNote: Sanitation-side counterpart to Section 5's EMP program — coordinate scoring.

requirements.title: Chemical storage separated to prevent odor/residue transfer
requirements.statement: Sanitation chemical storage and use areas are separated from cannabis product storage/handling areas sufficient to prevent chemical odor or residue transfer to finished product.
requirements.states: CO, CA, WA, MO, AR (universal best practice)
requirements.source: Derived — grounded in cannabis product**'**s odor/terpene-absorption characteristic
requirements.auditorNote: No conventional food-GMP analog. Flag chemical storage adjacent to open product bins or curing rooms.

requirements.title: Written EMP plan
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a written Environmental Monitoring Program (EMP) plan defining target organisms (minimum: Listeria species/Listeria monocytogenes indicator, Salmonella where applicable), sampling sites, sampling frequency, and laboratory methodology.
requirements.source: FDA Environmental Monitoring guidance; MFI EMP program expectation
requirements.auditorNote: Use documented EMP zone-map maturity structure as the internal benchmark.

requirements.title: Zone-mapped sampling sites
requirements.statement: EMP sampling sites are mapped and classified by zone (Zone 1-4), with a written zone map maintained and reviewed at least annually.
requirements.source: FDA EMP guidance zone methodology; cross-references 2.08
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 2.08.

requirements.title: Risk-based sampling frequency
requirements.statement: EMP sampling frequency is risk-based and no less than the minimum defined in the written plan; high-risk Zone 1/Zone 2 sites are sampled at a frequency sufficient to detect resident-pathogen establishment.
requirements.auditorNote: Frequency should escalate in response to findings, not remain static.

requirements.title: Accredited laboratory testing
requirements.statement: Facility uses an accredited third-party laboratory (or internally validated equivalent method) for EMP pathogen testing, with turnaround time sufficient to support timely corrective action.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the lab's accreditation scope includes the target organism/matrix (cannabis-specific interference risk).

requirements.title: Defined positive-result corrective action
requirements.statement: Facility maintains defined corrective action procedures for positive EMP results, including enhanced cleaning/sanitizing, root-cause investigation, expanded/vector sampling, and product disposition evaluation.
requirements.auditorNote: Coordinate scoring with 4.13 to avoid double-counting.

requirements.title: EMP trend analysis reviewed by management
requirements.statement: EMP results (positive and negative) are trended over time, with trend analysis reviewed as part of management review to identify recurring positive sites or increasing positivity rates.
requirements.source: Standard food-manufacturing EMP trending practice; cross-references 1.06
requirements.auditorNote: Ask to see the trend analysis output itself, not just raw inspection sheets.

requirements.title: Escalated response to resident-positive sites
requirements.statement: A resident-positive site (repeated positive result at the same location after corrective action) triggers an escalated investigation, including consideration of harborage points, equipment modification, or decommissioning if remediation fails.
requirements.auditorNote: A facility claiming zero positives across years of testing should be scrutinized for under-sampling.

requirements.title: Risk-appropriate finished/in-process product testing
requirements.statement: Finished product or in-process product testing (pathogen or indicator organism) is conducted at a frequency and scope appropriate to the product's risk profile.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — risk-based food safety testing principle
requirements.auditorNote: Distinguish clearly from mandatory state potency/pesticide/heavy-metal testing in Section 9.

requirements.title: Documented water-activity/moisture risk assessment
requirements.statement: Facility conducts a documented water activity (aw) or moisture content risk assessment for each product formulation to determine appropriate EMP/testing rigor and shelf-life/storage requirements.
requirements.auditorNote: Flagged for Phase 1 hardening — WA's exact water activity numeric limits need full regulatory-text verification.

requirements.title: Trained aseptic sampling technique
requirements.statement: Employees involved in EMP sampling are trained in aseptic sampling technique to prevent false-positive contamination from improper swabbing practice.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask the sampler to walk through their technique verbally as a practical test.

requirements.title: Harborage-site coverage in sampling rotation
requirements.statement: EMP sampling site rotation includes coverage of infrequently cleaned or hard-to-reach harborage-prone locations (drains, condensate lines, equipment framework, wheels/casters) in addition to routine high-visibility sites.
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-check the full site list against actual drain/framework locations observed on the floor.

requirements.title: Licensed PCO or qualified in-house program
requirements.statement: Facility contracts with a licensed pest control operator (PCO) or maintains an equivalently qualified in-house pest management program, with current licensure/certification on file.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify PCO license is current and jurisdiction-specific; some states require separate applicator licensing near cannabis product.

requirements.title: Current, reconciled device map
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a current pest control device map identifying the location and type of all monitoring/control devices, reconciled against the physical facility layout.
requirements.auditorNote: Walk a sample of mapped device locations to confirm placement matches the map.

requirements.title: Contamination-safe device placement
requirements.statement: Pest control devices are not placed in a manner that creates a risk of product, ingredient, or packaging contamination.
requirements.auditorNote: Insect light traps over exposed product staging is a recurring finding.

requirements.title: Approved, licensed pesticide application
requirements.statement: Pesticides used for structural/facility pest control are approved for use in a food-handling environment and applied only by licensed applicators, in accordance with label restrictions.
requirements.auditorNote: Distinguish from cannabis cultivation pesticide-residue testing addressed in Section 9.

requirements.title: Trended pest activity logs
requirements.statement: Facility maintains pest activity trend logs (device inspection results, catch counts, activity by location) reviewed at a defined frequency to identify emerging infestation risk.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask to see the trend analysis output itself, not just raw inspection sheets.

requirements.title: Corrective action for confirmed pest findings
requirements.statement: Facility has a documented corrective action process for confirmed pest activity findings, including root-cause investigation and verification of corrective action effectiveness.
requirements.auditorNote: Trace the most recent actual pest finding through to closure.

requirements.title: Employee pest-awareness training
requirements.statement: Employees are trained to recognize and report signs of pest activity as part of routine GMP awareness.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask a floor-level employee what they'd do if they saw evidence of rodent activity.

requirements.title: Receiving inspection for pest evidence
requirements.statement: Incoming raw cannabis material and other ingredients are inspected upon receipt for evidence of pest infestation prior to acceptance into production.
requirements.auditorNote: Coordinate scoring with Section 9's receiving-inspection control.

requirements.title: Physical exclusion as the primary control layer
requirements.statement: Facility maintains adequate physical exclusion as the primary pest-prevention layer, with chemical/mechanical control treated as a secondary, verification-based layer rather than the sole control.
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 2.06.

requirements.title: Cannabis-specific pest/pathogen receiving criteria
requirements.statement: Where cannabis-specific pests present a risk to incoming raw material quality, the facility's receiving inspection criteria explicitly address these pest/pathogen indicators, distinct from generic stored-product-pest inspection criteria.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify receiving staff are trained to distinguish cannabis-specific pest/mold indicators from generic stored-product evidence.

title: Water, Air, Steam & Compressed Gas Quality

requirements.title: Safe, adequate water source
requirements.statement: Water used in food production (as an ingredient, for cleaning food-contact surfaces, or for handwashing) is from a safe and adequate source, meeting applicable safe drinking water standards.
requirements.auditorNote: For well-water facilities, verify testing frequency matches or exceeds municipal-supply equivalency.

requirements.title: Potability testing at defined frequency
requirements.statement: Facility maintains water potability testing records at a defined frequency (minimum annual for municipal supply; more frequent for private well sources), with results within safe drinking water parameters.
requirements.auditorNote: Benchmark against daily chlorine residual + quarterly full potability panel for well-sourced facilities.

requirements.title: Monitored on-site treatment systems
requirements.statement: Where water is treated on-site (chlorination, UV, filtration, reverse osmosis) prior to use, treatment system function is monitored and verified at a defined frequency, with residual/output levels recorded.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify contemporaneous, non-repetitive readings.

requirements.title: Cross-connection/backflow control
requirements.statement: Cross-connection control is in place to prevent backflow/back-siphonage of non-potable water, chemicals, or wastewater into the potable water supply.
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 2.10.

requirements.title: Potable ice handling
requirements.statement: Ice used in contact with food (if applicable) is made from potable water and is handled/stored to prevent contamination.
requirements.auditorNote: Applicable primarily to infused-beverage processors using ice in filling/cooling steps.

requirements.title: Filtered/treated process gases
requirements.statement: Compressed air and other process gases (nitrogen, CO2) that contact food or food-contact surfaces are filtered/treated to prevent contamination.
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 3.07.

requirements.title: Food/beverage-grade extraction CO2
requirements.statement: CO2 used in supercritical or subcritical extraction is food/beverage-grade and sourced from a supplier providing a current Certificate of Analysis confirming purity specifications.
requirements.source: Standard extraction-industry input-quality practice; cross-references Section 9
requirements.auditorNote: Coordinate with Section 9's supplier/COA program.

requirements.title: HVAC preventing condensation and airborne contamination
requirements.statement: HVAC systems serving production areas are designed and maintained to prevent condensation dripping onto product/food-contact surfaces, and are filtered/maintained to minimize introduction of airborne contaminants.
requirements.auditorNote: Score in coordination with 2.05.

requirements.title: Segregated air-handling between cultivation/curing and manufacturing
requirements.statement: Where the facility's HVAC/air-handling system is shared or interconnected between cannabis cultivation/curing areas and infused-product manufacturing areas, air-handling separation or filtration is sufficient to prevent cross-contamination between zones.
requirements.auditorNote: Priority item for vertically integrated operators; no conventional food-facility analog.

requirements.title: Food-grade steam where used
requirements.statement: Steam, where used as a direct or indirect food-contact heating medium, is generated using potable water and treated with only food-grade boiler additives, with no contact between food-grade steam lines and non-food-grade boiler treatment chemicals.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify boiler additive SDS confirms food-grade/GRAS status.

requirements.title: Personal cleanliness standards
requirements.statement: Personnel working in direct contact with food, food-contact surfaces, or food-packaging materials maintain adequate personal cleanliness (clean outer garments, hair restraints, no jewelry other than plain wedding bands in exposed-product areas).
requirements.auditorNote: Watch specifically for rings/watches at hand-contact points on packaging lines.

requirements.title: Adequate, used handwashing facilities
requirements.statement: Handwashing facilities are conveniently located, adequately supplied, and personnel wash hands at appropriate points (upon entry, after breaks, after using the restroom, after handling waste).
requirements.auditorNote: Directly observe an actual entry/re-entry event rather than relying on posted signage.

requirements.title: Restricted-item policy including personal cannabis use
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a policy restricting food, gum, tobacco products (including personal cannabis consumption), and personal beverages to designated non-production areas, enforced consistently.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the policy explicitly addresses employee cannabis use/impairment during work hours.

requirements.title: Illness reporting and exclusion
requirements.statement: Personnel exhibiting symptoms of illness are excluded from operations that could result in product contamination, per a documented illness-reporting and exclusion policy.
requirements.auditorNote: Interview a floor supervisor about the actual exclusion process and return-to-work criteria.

requirements.title: Documented, verified GMP training
requirements.statement: Facility maintains documented GMP/food-safety training for all personnel prior to starting work in production areas, with refresher training at a defined frequency (minimum annual) and training effectiveness verification.
requirements.auditorNote: Request training records for recently hired employees specifically.

requirements.title: Current, verified cannabis handler licensure
requirements.statement: Personnel handling cannabis products maintain any state-required cannabis handler permit/license/badge, current and specific to the role performed, verified against the state's public registry where available.
requirements.auditorNote: Hard licensing gate — no food-GMP analog. Unlicensed handlers is a critical compliance failure independent of food-safety performance.

requirements.title: Cannabis-specific safety training for extraction/concentrate roles
requirements.statement: Personnel are trained on cannabis-specific safety considerations relevant to their role (solvent handling/extraction safety, cannabinoid exposure/overexposure symptoms, PPE requirements for concentrate handling).
requirements.auditorNote: Overlaps with OSHA obligations; treated here as a leading indicator of operational culture.

requirements.title: Visitor/contractor GMP orientation
requirements.statement: Visitors and contractors entering production areas follow the same GMP/hygiene requirements as employees, and are provided a brief orientation prior to entry.
requirements.auditorNote: Observe your own entry process as the auditor as a live test.

requirements.title: Training matrix mapped to roles with gap remediation
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented employee training matrix mapping required training topics to roles, with a mechanism to identify and remediate training gaps.
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-check the matrix against actual floor assignments.

requirements.title: Task-appropriate gloving with change policy
requirements.statement: Personnel handling exposed product wear gloves appropriate to the task, with a documented glove-change policy and glove material appropriate to the process.
requirements.auditorNote: Watch for glove reuse across zone transitions.

requirements.title: Documented approved supplier program
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented approved supplier program for all raw material, ingredient, and packaging suppliers, with defined approval criteria and periodic reapproval/reassessment.
requirements.source: 21 CFR 117.410; MFI Supplier Expectation Manual (direct analog)
requirements.auditorNote: Direct structural analog to the MFI supplier program.

requirements.title: Commercially manufactured non-cannabis ingredients
requirements.statement: With the exception of cannabis itself, all ingredients used in oral-ingestion infused products are sourced as commercially manufactured food from licensed/regulated food sources, not homemade or unregulated inputs.
requirements.states: WA (explicit); UNIV best practice elsewhere pending verification
requirements.auditorNote: Flagged for Phase 1 verification of an equivalent rule in CO/CA/MO.

requirements.title: Current COAs/specification sheets on file
requirements.statement: Non-cannabis ingredient suppliers provide current Certificates of Analysis (COA) and/or specification sheets verifying identity, quality, and safety parameters relevant to the ingredient's use.
requirements.auditorNote: Sample a cross-section of COAs against actual specification requirements.

requirements.title: Licensed-source cannabis input with chain of custody
requirements.statement: Cannabis/hemp biomass, flower, or extract inputs are received only from licensed cultivators/processors, with chain-of-custody documentation verified against the state's seed-to-sale tracking system at receipt.
requirements.source: State track-and-trace system requirements (METRC, BioTrack, etc.)
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-reference the physical delivery against the electronic manifest number-for-number.

requirements.title: Lot-verified compliance testing prior to release
requirements.statement: Each incoming lot of cannabis/hemp input is verified against its required state-mandated compliance testing (potency, pesticide residue, heavy metals, microbial/mycotoxin, residual solvent) prior to release into production, with test results retained and traceable to the specific lot.
requirements.source: State-mandated cannabis compliance testing panels (varies by state)
requirements.auditorNote: Flagged for Phase 1 hardening to build the full state-by-state analyte matrix.

requirements.title: Documented failed-test disposition process
requirements.statement: Facility has a documented process for evaluating and responding to out-of-specification or failed compliance testing results on incoming cannabis inputs, including hold, reject, and (where permitted) remediation procedures.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the facility's stated remediation practice is actually permitted under current state rule.

requirements.title: Certified child-resistant packaging suppliers
requirements.statement: Packaging material suppliers (including child-resistant packaging components) provide documentation confirming compliance with applicable state child-resistant packaging certification standards prior to use.
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-references Section 14 finished-package verification.

requirements.title: Ongoing supplier performance monitoring
requirements.statement: Facility conducts and documents periodic supplier performance monitoring as part of ongoing supplier reassessment, not solely at initial approval.
requirements.source: MFI ongoing supplier monitoring expectation (direct analog)
requirements.auditorNote: Request evidence of a supplier removed or placed on probation based on performance history.

requirements.title: Risk-based approach to unverifiable lab COAs
requirements.statement: Where a supplier COA cannot be independently verified against a state's public licensing/testing-lab-accreditation database, the facility has a documented risk-based approach for evaluating and documenting acceptance of that supplier relationship.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — documented industry lab-accreditation-integrity concerns
requirements.auditorNote: Ask directly how the facility would know if their testing lab's results were unreliable.

requirements.title: Full supplier/ingredient lot traceability
requirements.statement: Facility maintains full traceability linking each finished product lot back to specific incoming cannabis input lot(s), non-cannabis ingredient lot(s), and packaging lot(s) used, sufficient to support a one-step-forward/one-step-back trace exercise.
requirements.source: 21 CFR 117.310; state track-and-trace lot-linkage requirements; cross-references Section 15
requirements.auditorNote: Verifies the underlying data exists; Section 15 verifies actual trace execution.

requirements.title: Written hazard analysis addressing cannabis-specific hazards
requirements.statement: Facility has conducted and documented a written hazard analysis identifying known or reasonably foreseeable biological, chemical, and physical hazards for each product/process, consistent with 21 CFR 117 Subpart C methodology.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify explicit inclusion of cannabis-specific chemical hazards (residual solvent, pesticide carryover, heavy-metal uptake).

requirements.title: PCQI-overseen, periodically reassessed analysis
requirements.statement: Hazard analysis is conducted or overseen by a qualified individual and is reviewed/reassessed upon any change to ingredients, process, equipment, or at minimum every three years.
requirements.auditorNote: Confirm the reassessment trigger list explicitly includes cannabis-specific changes.

requirements.title: Preventive controls mapped to every identified hazard
requirements.statement: Preventive controls (process, food allergen, sanitation, supply-chain) are identified for each hazard requiring a preventive control, with associated parameters and monitoring procedures documented.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify every identified hazard resolves to a specific, monitored preventive control.

requirements.title: Documented process preventive control parameters
requirements.statement: Process preventive controls include defined critical parameters with established critical limits, monitoring frequency, and documented monitoring records.
requirements.auditorNote: Apply the same rigor used for conventional food process control points.

requirements.title: Sanitation preventive controls cross-referenced to Sections 4-5
requirements.statement: Sanitation preventive controls (where identified as necessary to control an environmental pathogen hazard) are documented with monitoring, corrective action, and verification procedures, cross-referencing Sections 4 and 5.
requirements.auditorNote: Score plan documentation here; operational execution in Sections 4/5.

requirements.title: Supply-chain preventive controls cross-referenced to Section 9
requirements.statement: Supply-chain preventive controls (where identified as necessary to control a hazard that will be controlled by a supplier) are documented, with defined supplier verification activities appropriate to hazard risk.
requirements.auditorNote: Section 9's compliance testing functions as the supply-chain PC verification activity.

requirements.title: Written recall plan within the food safety plan
requirements.statement: A written recall plan exists as part of the food safety plan, consistent with 21 CFR 117.139, cross-referencing Section 15.
requirements.auditorNote: Score plan existence here; execution/mock recall performance in Section 15.

requirements.title: Signed, reassessed food safety plan
requirements.statement: The food safety plan is reviewed and re-analyzed as required upon triggering events and is signed/dated by the qualified individual who performed or oversaw its preparation.
requirements.auditorNote: Check the signature/date against the facility's actual operational timeline.

requirements.title: Documented verification activities
requirements.statement: Verification activities (validation of preventive controls, verification of monitoring, calibration verification, and records review) are documented consistent with 21 CFR 117.155-117.165.
requirements.auditorNote: Test the facility's understanding of validation vs. verification distinction in the closing interview.

requirements.title: Scientifically supported kill-step validation
requirements.statement: Where a kill-step or other validated control is relied upon to reduce a microbial or other hazard to an acceptable level, the validation study is scientifically supportable and specific to the facility's actual equipment and process parameters.
requirements.auditorNote: Do not accept an unvalidated assumption (e.g., decarb temperature profile) as equivalent to a documented kill-step validation.

requirements.title: Formal hazard determination on cannabinoid dose uniformity
requirements.statement: The facility's hazard analysis explicitly evaluates and documents a determination (with rationale) on whether cannabinoid content/potency variability constitutes a chemical hazard requiring a preventive control.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — logical extension of HARPC methodology
requirements.auditorNote: Most conceptually important contribution of the Canna-Safe Programs framework — no FDA guidance category for this.

requirements.title: Validated homogenization for uniform dispersion
requirements.statement: Cannabis-infused edible products in solid or liquid form are homogenized/mixed using a validated process to ensure uniform dispersion of cannabinoids throughout the product, preventing 'hot spots.'
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-references Section 3.09 equipment qualification.

requirements.title: Batch-release potency and analyte testing
requirements.statement: Each production batch is tested for cannabinoid potency (and other state-mandated analytes) by a licensed/accredited laboratory prior to release, with results retained and linked to the specific batch/lot.
requirements.auditorNote: Distinct from Section 9's incoming-material testing — this addresses the facility's own finished output.

requirements.title: Intra-batch uniformity testing beyond single-sample release
requirements.statement: Facility conducts intra-batch uniformity testing (multiple samples from different points within a single batch) at a defined frequency, in addition to a single batch-release potency test.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — beyond typical state release-testing minimum
requirements.auditorNote: Value-added service offering; a single release test can miss significant intra-batch variability.

requirements.title: Documented, verified batch-calculation methodology
requirements.statement: Where a product is formulated to a specific per-serving or per-package cannabinoid target, the facility's batch calculation methodology is documented and periodically verified against actual finished-product test results.
requirements.auditorNote: Formulation-methodology errors are an underappreciated root cause of potency-labeling non-conformance.

requirements.title: Documented failed-batch disposition process
requirements.statement: Facility has a documented process for evaluating and dispositioning finished product lots that fail potency, uniformity, or other release testing, including hold, destruction, or (where permitted) reformulation/rework procedures.
requirements.auditorNote: Coordinate with Section 9.06 — verify the facility distinguishes incoming-material vs. finished-product disposition.

requirements.title: Monitored infusion-specific critical parameters
requirements.statement: Process critical parameters specific to infusion methodology (decarboxylation temperature/time profile, emulsification parameters, encapsulation/nanoemulsion process parameters) are monitored and recorded for each batch, with defined critical limits.
requirements.auditorNote: Operationalizes 10.04 specifically for infusion technology.

requirements.title: Substantiated shelf-life/stability claims
requirements.statement: Facility maintains documented shelf-life/stability data supporting labeled cannabinoid content remaining within acceptable tolerance through the product's stated shelf life.
requirements.states: UNIV (best practice; mandate varies by state)
requirements.auditorNote: Flagged for Phase 1 hardening — verify whether any target state has an explicit shelf-life/stability mandate.

requirements.title: Traceable, dosage-safe rework practices
requirements.statement: Rework or reprocessed material (off-spec batches reincorporated into new production) is tracked with full traceability to originating batch(es), and reincorporation does not result in a finished product exceeding any single-batch dosage cap or violating labeling accuracy tolerances.
requirements.auditorNote: Elevated risk relative to conventional food rework due to the dosage-cap dimension.

requirements.title: Per-serving/per-package THC dosage caps
requirements.statement: Cannabis-infused food/drink products do not exceed the state-defined maximum THC per serving and per package; serving sizes are accurately and consistently dosed.
requirements.source: AR NORML summary; WA DOH medical standard
requirements.auditorNote: Distinguish adult-use vs. medical dosage caps where a state has both tracks.

requirements.title: No child-appealing product design or packaging
requirements.statement: Cannabis-infused edible products are not designed, shaped, or packaged in a manner that resembles non-cannabis products primarily consumed by and marketed to children.
requirements.source: AR NORML summary; CA DCC packaging rules; CO packaging rules
requirements.auditorNote: Apply as a universal packaging/product-design checkpoint given consistent child-safety rationale.

requirements.title: No consumer cooking/baking required (WA)
requirements.statement: Cannabis-infused food or drink products do not require cooking or baking by the consumer prior to consumption (product is sold ready-to-consume).
requirements.auditorNote: Straightforward label-review check.

requirements.title: Dual-agency recipe approval (WA)
requirements.statement: All recipes for cannabis-infused products meant for oral ingestion are submitted for and receive approval from the state Department of Agriculture (or equivalent) prior to submission for packaging/label review by the cannabis regulatory board; approved recipe is kept on file.
requirements.auditorNote: Confirm both approvals (WSDA recipe + LCB product/label) exist, not just LCB-side approval.

requirements.title: No prohibited frozen dessert/acidified food categories (MO)
requirements.statement: Facility does not manufacture cannabis-infused frozen desserts or acidified foods (as defined by the state's food code), which are categorically prohibited regardless of process controls.
requirements.auditorNote: Hard category exclusion — binary pass/fail, not a risk-managed permission.

requirements.title: No infusion into TCS foods (WA)
requirements.statement: Facility does not infuse cannabis into potentially hazardous foods (time/temperature control for safety, or 'TCS' foods) that require time-temperature control to prevent pathogen growth or toxin production.
requirements.auditorNote: Hard category exclusion specific to WA — code as binary pass/fail.

requirements.title: Compliant alcohol-containing tinctures
requirements.statement: Tinctures and other alcohol-containing infused products comply with applicable state alcohol-content limits and any dual-licensure requirements where alcohol content triggers additional regulatory oversight beyond the cannabis license alone.
requirements.states: CA (explicit flag); CO, WA, MO, AR (verify)
requirements.auditorNote: Flagged since original workbook — prioritize full-text verification before live CA tincture-client audit.

requirements.title: Topical products correctly excluded from ingestible pathway
requirements.statement: Topical cannabis products comply with applicable state cosmetic/topical-specific labeling and formulation requirements, distinct from the ingestible-product (food) regulatory pathway, and are not represented as having ingestible/oral-consumption use.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the facility's product mix at audit scoping to apply correct category logic throughout the whole framework.

requirements.title: Current beverage-specific regulatory compliance
requirements.statement: Beverage-category infused products comply with any state-specific carbonation, alcohol-analog, or beverage-specific labeling requirements.
requirements.auditorNote: Fastest-evolving regulatory subcategory across all target states — verify current rule at audit time.

requirements.title: Substantiated health/wellness claims
requirements.statement: Facility maintains documentation supporting any health, wellness, or functional claims made on infused-product labeling or marketing materials, consistent with state restrictions on unsubstantiated medical/therapeutic claims.
requirements.auditorNote: Flag any 'treats,' 'cures,' or 'prevents' language for immediate escalation.

requirements.title: Current major-allergen identification including sesame
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a written allergen control plan identifying all major food allergens (milk, egg, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, sesame) present in any ingredient, product, or shared production line.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the plan reflects sesame as a major allergen (older templates may not).

requirements.title: Physical/procedural allergen segregation in storage
requirements.statement: Allergen-containing ingredients are physically or procedurally segregated from non-allergen ingredients during storage to prevent cross-contact.
requirements.auditorNote: Check vertical as well as horizontal storage separation.

requirements.title: Validated shared-line changeover cleaning
requirements.statement: Where shared production equipment/lines are used for both allergen-containing and allergen-free products, a validated changeover cleaning procedure is in place and verified before allergen-free production resumes.
requirements.auditorNote: Request the validation study for the highest-risk shared-line scenario, not just the SSOP.

requirements.title: Accurate allergen labeling matching formulation
requirements.statement: Finished product labeling accurately declares all major food allergens present, using compliant 'Contains' statement or ingredient-list bolding/parenthetical declaration.
requirements.auditorNote: Cross-reference the finished-product label against formulation records including sub-ingredients.

requirements.title: Risk-based precautionary labeling
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented allergen risk assessment for each product formulation, evaluating precautionary 'may contain' labeling appropriateness based on actual cross-contact risk.
requirements.source: Standard food-manufacturing allergen risk assessment practice
requirements.auditorNote: Reflexive 'may contain' labeling on every product signals the underlying assessment wasn't used to drive labeling decisions.

requirements.title: Product-specific allergen awareness training
requirements.statement: Employee training explicitly covers allergen awareness, cross-contact prevention practices, and the specific allergens present in the facility's product portfolio.
requirements.auditorNote: Ask a line employee to name the specific allergen(s) present in what they're currently producing.

requirements.title: Sub-ingredient-level allergen evaluation for flavors/colors
requirements.statement: Non-cannabis flavoring, coloring, and functional ingredients are evaluated for allergen content at the sub-ingredient level, not assumed allergen-free based on the finished-ingredient name alone.
requirements.auditorNote: Request full sub-ingredient breakdown documentation from flavor/color suppliers.

requirements.title: Certified, verified child-resistant packaging
requirements.statement: Finished product packaging is child-resistant, certified to applicable state standard, with current certification documentation on file from the packaging supplier.
requirements.source: State CRP requirements referencing 16 CFR 1700.20; cross-references 9.07
requirements.auditorNote: Also requires physical verification that packaging in use matches the certified specification.

requirements.title: Label THC/CBD content matching test results within tolerance
requirements.statement: Finished product labeling accurately declares total THC/CBD content (and other state-required cannabinoids) per package and per serving, consistent with actual finished-product test results within the state's allowed labeling tolerance.
requirements.auditorNote: Directly cross-check label claim against actual batch-release COA (11.02) for current-production lots.

requirements.title: Current required warning statements
requirements.statement: Labeling includes all state-required warning statements in the required format, size, and placement.
requirements.auditorNote: Frequently revised — verify current rule at each audit.

requirements.title: Current universal symbol
requirements.statement: Universal cannabis symbol (state-specific standardized THC/warning symbol, where required) is present on packaging in the required size and placement.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the specific symbol design in use matches the state's current approved symbol.

requirements.title: Durable, traceable lot identification
requirements.statement: Package labeling includes lot/batch identification sufficient to support traceability, printed legibly and durably.
requirements.source: 21 CFR 117.310; state track-and-trace lot-identification requirements; cross-references Section 15
requirements.auditorNote: Physically test label durability where feasible.

requirements.title: Accurate net weight/volume declarations
requirements.statement: Net weight/volume declarations on packaging are accurate and comply with applicable weights-and-measures standards, verified periodically through facility self-checks.
requirements.auditorNote: Primarily a documentation-verification item.

requirements.title: Controlled pre-production label/artwork approval
requirements.statement: Packaging and labeling artwork undergoes a documented pre-production approval process prior to first use, with version control preventing use of outdated/unapproved artwork.
requirements.source: Standard label-control practice; state-specific label pre-approval requirements vary
requirements.auditorNote: Verify against Section 12.04's WA dual-agency requirement where applicable.

requirements.title: Change-controlled label updates
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a documented process for managing label/packaging changes that triggers timely re-verification of label accuracy and, where required, regulatory re-approval, before the revised product enters commerce.
requirements.auditorNote: Trace the facility's most recent actual label change through to re-approval.

requirements.title: State-compliant multi-serving package demarcation
requirements.statement: Where a product package contains multiple discrete servings, package-level THC content and per-serving demarcation meet state-specific requirements for consumer dose-control.
requirements.states: CO, CA, WA, MO, AR (verify per-state requirement)
requirements.auditorNote: Common point of state-to-state variation — flag explicitly as state-conditional.

requirements.title: Full one-step-forward/one-step-back traceability
requirements.statement: Facility maintains full lot traceability (one-step-forward/one-step-back) linking finished product lots to incoming cannabis input lots, non-cannabis ingredient lots, packaging lots, and outbound distribution records.
requirements.auditorNote: Verifies underlying data architecture; 15.03 verifies actual execution under time pressure.

requirements.title: Reconciliation with state track-and-trace system
requirements.statement: Facility's internal lot-traceability system is integrated with or reconciled against the state's mandatory seed-to-sale tracking system, such that internal records and state-system records agree for a given lot.
requirements.auditorNote: Pull a sample lot and independently verify against the state tracking system's record.

requirements.title: Semi-annual mock recall exercises with recovery-rate benchmark
requirements.statement: Facility conducts a documented mock recall exercise at a minimum semi-annual frequency, evaluating both speed and accuracy of the trace.
requirements.source: Standard food-manufacturing mock recall practice (≥95% recovery benchmark)
requirements.auditorNote: Apply the ≥95% effectiveness benchmark and semi-annual minimum frequency as the baseline standard.

requirements.title: Cannabis-specific mock recall scenarios
requirements.statement: Mock recall exercises test recall scenarios specific to cannabis-industry risk in addition to conventional food-safety recall scenarios.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — extends conventional mock recall practice
requirements.auditorNote: A mock recall program testing only conventional food scenarios is testing an incomplete risk picture.

requirements.title: Written recall plan with state regulatory notification
requirements.statement: Facility maintains a written recall plan defining recall initiation criteria, internal notification chain, external notification requirements, and recall effectiveness verification methodology.
requirements.auditorNote: Verify the external notification chain explicitly includes the state cannabis regulatory agency.

requirements.title: Defined recall severity classification
requirements.statement: Recall plan defines product classification/severity criteria to guide the urgency and scope of recall response appropriate to the hazard involved.
requirements.source: FDA recall classification methodology (Class I/II/III); cross-references Section 16 severity model
requirements.auditorNote: Use consistent severity terminology with the audit-finding-severity model.

requirements.title: Current downstream distribution records
requirements.statement: Facility maintains distribution records sufficient to identify all downstream recipients of each product lot, with contact information current and verified.
requirements.auditorNote: Sample-test a recent distribution record by attempting to verify the listed recipient's license/contact info is current.

requirements.title: Closed-loop corrective action on recall performance gaps
requirements.statement: Where the facility's mock recall or actual recall history reveals any recovery-rate or timeliness shortfall, root-cause analysis and corrective action are documented, with subsequent mock recall exercises specifically designed to test whether the corrective action resolved the gap.
requirements.auditorNote: An unmodified repeat exercise next cycle hasn't actually closed the loop.

title: Certification/Audit Program Governance, Corrective Actions & Continuous Improvement

requirements.title: Risk-adjusted audit frequency
requirements.statement: Canna-Safe Programs certification audits are scheduled at a defined base frequency (recommended annual minimum, consistent with CO's mandatory annual third-party cGMP audit requirement), with frequency adjustable upward based on documented risk factors.
requirements.source: CO hemp safe-harbor mandatory annual third-party audit requirement; MFI Audit Frequency Justification methodology (inverted)
requirements.auditorNote: Cannabis clients start at a higher-scrutiny baseline with justified reduction potential over time.

requirements.title: Defined finding severity model
requirements.statement: Audit findings are classified using a defined severity model (Critical / Major / Minor) with explicit criteria distinguishing each severity level.
requirements.auditorNote: Critical = imminent consumer-safety/license risk; Major = systemic latent-risk gap; Minor = isolated low-risk gap.

requirements.title: Certification hold on Critical findings pending closure
requirements.statement: Facility receiving a Critical finding is subject to immediate corrective action requirement with certification hold/suspension pending verified closure.
requirements.source: Derived program-governance rule; analog to FDA Class I recall urgency standard
requirements.auditorNote: Document clearly in the certification program manual before any finding occurs.

requirements.title: 5 C****'****s CAPA methodology
requirements.statement: Corrective Action/Preventive Action (CAPA) responses to audit findings follow a defined format: root-cause analysis, immediate correction, systemic corrective action, and verification-of-effectiveness evidence.
requirements.source: SQF Lead Auditor training — 5 C**'**s methodology
requirements.auditorNote: Direct methodological carryover from SQF Lead Auditor training.

requirements.title: Floor-time-weighted audit conduct
requirements.statement: Auditor time allocation during an on-site audit follows the same objective-evidence-gathering discipline established in SQF Lead Auditor training: a substantial majority of audit time spent on floor observations/interviews rather than solely document review.
requirements.source: SQF Lead Auditor training — 60/40 observation-time standard
requirements.auditorNote: Governs auditor conduct, not facility-side requirements.

requirements.title: Independent certification decision-making
requirements.statement: Certification decisions are made by a role functionally independent from the auditor who conducted the on-site assessment.
requirements.auditorNote: Relevant to Phase 2 accredited CB status — build the separation now to avoid later retrofit.

requirements.title: Independently verified corrective action closure
requirements.statement: Facility corrective action closure is independently verified by Canna-Safe Programs before certification status is restored or maintained — corrective action is not self-certified as closed by the facility alone.
requirements.source: Standard third-party certification governance principle; direct analog to MFI SCAR closure-verification role
requirements.auditorNote: Mirrors existing MFI/BEF SCAR policy discipline.

requirements.title: Tracked regulatory-currency governance mechanism
requirements.statement: Canna-Safe Programs maintains a documented process for monitoring and incorporating regulatory changes across all five target states into the audit program.
requirements.source: Derived program-governance requirement synthesizing the recurring **'**verify current rule**'** flags throughout the framework
requirements.auditorNote: Build a literal tracking document: citation, last-verified date, next-review-due date, responsible party.

requirements.title: Client feedback and program continuous improvement
requirements.statement: Facility (client) satisfaction and program effectiveness are periodically assessed and reviewed as part of Canna-Safe Programs' own continuous improvement process, distinct from the facility-side management review in Section 1.06.
requirements.auditorNote: Build now, even in Phase 1 consulting form, to support future Phase 2 accreditation evaluation.

requirements.title: Retained, accessible audit and certification records
requirements.statement: Canna-Safe Programs maintains records of all audits, findings, corrective actions, and certification decisions in a document control system consistent with the retention standards established in Section 1.10, and accessible for review in the event of a Phase 2 accreditation body assessment.
requirements.auditorNote: Closes the loop back to the framework's own governance origin point.

requirements.statement: Facility verifies that each testing laboratory it relies on for compliance release holds current ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation from a recognized accreditation body (A2LA, PJLA, ANAB, or equivalent), confirmed against the accreditation body's public registry rather than the lab's own representation.
requirements.auditorNote: Baseline competence signal — always verify independently, never accept a lab's self-issued certificate as sufficient evidence.

requirements.statement: Facility confirms the lab's accredited scope specifically covers the exact analyte, method, and product matrix being relied upon (e.g., pesticide residue testing in an infused-beverage matrix, not just cannabinoid potency in flower).
requirements.auditorNote: A lab can be validly accredited for one matrix/analyte combination while having no accreditation at all for another — scope, not accreditation status alone, is what matters.

requirements.statement: Facility identifies and documents the specific test method used by the lab for each analyte category (e.g., an AOAC Official Method, a state-mandated method, or a validated in-house method), and confirms the method matches what the facility's state regulator requires for compliance release.
requirements.source: AOAC International Official Methods; state-specific mandated testing methods
requirements.auditorNote: State cannabis programs increasingly specify required methods by name — verify the lab's actual method matches the current state requirement, not an older or substitute method.

requirements.statement: Where a lab uses a non-AOAC, in-house, or otherwise non-standard method, the facility obtains and reviews the lab's method validation study (accuracy, precision, limit of detection/quantitation, and matrix-specific validation) before relying on that method for compliance release.
requirements.auditorNote: The single most commonly skipped verification step — labs frequently assert a method is 'validated' without being able to produce the underlying study on request.

requirements.statement: Facility confirms the lab participates in a recognized interlaboratory proficiency testing (PT) program for the relevant analytes, with recent passing results, reviewed at least annually.
requirements.auditorNote: PT performance is a real-world check on the lab's actual output quality, distinct from its paper accreditation status.

requirements.statement: Facility verifies the lab holds current state-required cannabis testing laboratory licensure/registration in the specific state where results will be used for compliance release, separate from and in addition to ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation.
requirements.source: State-specific cannabis testing laboratory licensing requirements
requirements.auditorNote: A lab can be fully ISO-accredited and still be unlicensed for cannabis compliance testing in a specific state — the two credentials are independent and both must be checked.

requirements.statement: Facility confirms the lab maintains a documented chain-of-custody process for sample intake, including sample origin, collector identity, transport conditions, and all custody transfer points, from collection through final result reporting.
requirements.auditorNote: Breaks in custody undermine the evidentiary value of an otherwise-passing result and are a documented vector for sample substitution or manipulation.

requirements.statement: Facility periodically cross-checks lab results against an independent retest (a different accredited lab testing a split or reserve sample from the same batch) at a defined frequency, with results reviewed for material discrepancy.
requirements.source: Derived requirement — addresses documented industry lab-integrity risk
requirements.auditorNote: Directly closes the lab-fraud risk already flagged at requirement 9.09. Inflated potency and false-pass results have been the subject of documented state enforcement actions against labs in multiple markets.

requirements.statement: Facility confirms no ownership, financial, or other conflict-of-interest relationship exists between the testing laboratory and the facility, or between the lab and any entity providing financial backing to the facility.
requirements.auditorNote: Easy to overlook with smaller regional labs in tighter-knit state markets — ask directly rather than assuming independence.

requirements.statement: Facility reviews the lab's Certificate of Analysis (COA) format for completeness: method reference cited, limit of detection/quantitation stated where applicable, sample ID traceable to the specific batch, and analyst/reviewer sign-off present.
requirements.auditorNote: A COA missing method reference or LOD/LOQ values is a red flag for reporting rigor even before any result is examined substantively. Page of Page of
